## Purpose

This SOP describes the specifications, assembly, maintenance, and
ordering of replacement parts for the Price Pygmy and Price Type AA
mechanical current meters used by the EA Program. These vertical-axis
cup-type meters convert water velocity into rotational counts and are
the standard instruments for measuring point velocities during stream
discharge measurements [@rantz1982] (see also
[SOP-F301 Stream Discharge Measurement](SOP-F301-stream-discharge-measurement.qmd)).


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Price Pygmy current meters and Price Type AA current
  meters owned by the EA Program, including standard cat-whisker and
  magnetic-head contact chamber variants
- **Does not apply to:** Electronic velocity meters (e.g.,
  Marsh-McBirney, FlowTracker ADV), propeller-type meters (e.g., Ott),
  or acoustic Doppler instruments
- **Location:** Instruments stored in the EA field equipment room;
  maintenance performed in SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                         |
|:------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve purchases, authorize meter retirement          |
| Field Lead        | Perform pre-field spin tests, coordinate maintenance   |
| Trained Personnel | Assemble, inspect, and clean meters per this SOP       |
| New Students      | Complete training before handling meters               |


## Definitions

- **AquaCalc:** A digital flow computer that counts current meter
  revolutions electronically and converts them to velocity
  automatically using the stored rating table; eliminates manual
  timing and reduces transcription error.
- **Cat-whisker contact:** A spring-wire contact element in the Type AA
  meter's contact chamber; makes electrical contact with a solder bead
  on the shaft once per revolution (single-revolution contact) or once
  per five revolutions (penta contact); must be checked for wear and
  proper contact force before each field season [@rantz1982].
- **Contact chamber:** The sealed housing on the Type AA meter that
  contains the electrical contact mechanism (cat-whisker wire and
  solder bead, or magnetic head); connects to the cable leading to the
  headset or digital counter.
- **Penta contact:** A gear-reduction contact in the Type AA meter
  that closes the circuit once every five bucket-wheel revolutions;
  used at high velocities to reduce the counting rate to a manageable
  level; not available on the Pygmy meter [@rantz1982].
- **Pivot:** The tungsten carbide tip at the bottom of the current
  meter shaft; rides in a hardened bearing cup; the single most
  wear-sensitive part of a mechanical current meter; must be inspected
  for burrs, flat spots, and magnetization before each field season
  [@rantz1982; @usgs_meterma].
- **Price Pygmy current meter:** A vertical-axis cup-type current
  meter with a 2-inch (5.1 cm) diameter bucket wheel; designed for
  shallow streams (depth ≤ 1.0 ft); wading rod suspension only; rated
  for velocities of 0.1--4.9 ft/s [@rantz1982].
- **Price Type AA current meter:** The standard USGS vertical-axis
  cup-type current meter with a 5-inch (12.7 cm) diameter bucket
  wheel; rated for velocities of 0.1--25 ft/s; can be suspended from
  a wading rod or cable [@rantz1982].
- **Rating table:** A lookup table, supplied with each meter by the
  manufacturer and approved by the USGS, that converts bucket-wheel
  revolutions per second to velocity in ft/s or m/s; laminated copies
  must be kept in each meter's carrying case [@rantz1982].
- **Raising nut:** The nut that controls the vertical position of the
  shaft and pivot within the yoke; must be tightened to the correct
  end-play setting (~0.001 in) for accurate measurements; never loosen
  by holding the nut and spinning the bucket wheel.
- **Spin test:** A field quality control check in which the bucket
  wheel is given a sharp spin by hand and the time for it to stop is
  measured; a proxy for bearing condition; minimum acceptable spin
  times are 40 s (Type AA) and 24 s (Pygmy) at room temperature
  [@rantz1982].
- **Wading rod (top-setting):** A graduated aluminum rod used to
  position the current meter at a known depth fraction (0.6 or 0.2/0.8
  of total depth) below the water surface; the depth-setting mechanism
  is located on the handle, enabling depth changes without removing the
  meter from the water.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Pivot points and shaft tips are sharp; handle with
  care. The bucket wheel can pinch fingers if spun while adjusting
  the assembly.
- **Chemical:** Instrument oil is a mild skin irritant. Avoid eye
  contact.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when oiling or cleaning with solvents)
- [ ] Safety glasses (when using compressed air for cleaning)


## Instrument Specifications

### Price Type AA Current Meter

The Type AA is the standard USGS Price-type current meter for general
streamflow measurement [@rantz1982]. The bucket wheel has six conical
cups (12.7 cm diameter) rotating on a vertical axis inside a brass
yoke. Tungsten carbide bearings are seated in deeply recessed inverted
cups that trap air and exclude water and silt. A tailpiece assembly
aligns the meter with the current when suspended by cable.

| Parameter              | Value                                      |
|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Velocity range         | 0.1--25 ft/s (0.03--7.6 m/s)              |
| Bucket wheel diameter  | 5 in (12.7 cm)                             |
| Number of cups         | 6                                          |
| Contact types          | Single revolution and penta (every 5 rev)  |
| Suspension             | Wading rod or cable with sounding weight   |
| Construction           | Brass and stainless steel, chrome plated   |
| Rating                 | USGS standard rating table (two equations joined at 1 rev/s = 2.2 ft/s) [@rantz1982] |

### Price Pygmy Current Meter

The Pygmy meter is scaled to two-fifths the size of the Type AA,
designed for shallow streams [@rantz1982]. The contact chamber is
integral to the yoke; single-revolution contact only (no penta gear).
The meter has no tailpiece and cannot be used with cable suspension.

| Parameter              | Value                                      |
|:-----------------------|:-------------------------------------------|
| Velocity range         | 0.1--4.9 ft/s (0.03--1.5 m/s)             |
| Bucket wheel diameter  | 2 in (5.1 cm)                              |
| Number of cups         | 6                                          |
| Contact type           | Single revolution only                     |
| Suspension             | Wading rod only (no cable suspension)      |
| Construction           | Brass and stainless steel, chrome plated   |
| Rating                 | USGS standard rating table (single equation) [@rantz1982] |

### Choosing Between Meters

| Condition                                  | Meter to Use |
|:-------------------------------------------|:-------------|
| Water depth > 1.0 ft (0.3 m)              | Type AA      |
| Water depth ≤ 1.0 ft (0.3 m)              | Pygmy        |
| Velocities expected > 4.9 ft/s            | Type AA      |
| Shallow stream edges (supplemental data)   | Pygmy        |
| Cable suspension required                  | Type AA      |

## Procedure

### Assembly

**Type AA on a wading rod:**

1. Remove the tailpiece assembly (used for cable suspension only).
2. Slide the meter yoke onto the wading rod and secure with the
   thumbscrew.
3. Connect the electrical cable from the binding posts on the contact
   chamber to the AquaCalc or headset.
4. For penta contact, connect to the penta binding post; for
   single-revolution counting, use the single-revolution binding post.

**Pygmy on a wading rod:**

1. Slide the pygmy yoke directly onto the wading rod and secure with
   the thumbscrew.
2. Connect the electrical cable to the binding post. The Pygmy has
   only a single-revolution contact.

### Pre-Field Spin Test

Perform a spin test before every field outing [@rantz1982]. Conduct
with the meter level, shaft vertical, in a location with no air
currents.

1. Hold the meter steady and use your finger or a pencil to give the
   bucket wheel a sharp, single spin.
2. Immediately start a stopwatch.
3. Stop the stopwatch when the wheel completely stops rotating.
4. Record the spin time in the field notebook.

Minimum acceptable spin times [@rantz1982]:

| Meter    | Minimum Spin Time | Optimum Spin Time |
|:---------|:------------------|:------------------|
| Type AA  | 40 s              | 60--120 s         |
| Pygmy    | 24 s              | 40--80 s          |

If the spin time falls below the minimum, clean and oil the pivot
before proceeding (§7.3). If the spin time remains low after cleaning
and oiling, replace the pivot.

### Cleaning and Oiling (Pre-Season and As Needed)

1. **Inspect the pivot.** Remove the raising nut and carefully withdraw
   the shaft. Examine the pivot tip under a magnifying glass. A good
   pivot is highly polished, with no flat spots, pits, or scratches.
   Replace a damaged pivot immediately.
2. **Check for magnetization.** Hold the pivot near a paper clip. If
   the clip is attracted to the pivot, the pivot is magnetized and will
   cause erroneously high velocity readings. Demagnetize using a bulk
   magnetic tape eraser.
3. **Oil the bearings.** Apply one small drop of instrument oil to the
   upper shaft bearing and one drop to the pivot. Do not over-oil;
   excess oil attracts grit.
4. **Inspect the bucket wheel.** Spin the wheel slowly and watch for
   wobble. If the upper hub wobbles more than the lower, the shaft is
   bent and must be replaced.
5. **Inspect the contact chamber.** For cat-whisker contacts, check
   that the wire makes clean contact with the solder bead on each
   revolution. For magnetic-head contacts, verify the counter registers
   properly during the spin test.

::: {.callout-warning}
### Raising Nut Caution
Never loosen the raising nut by holding the nut and spinning the
bucket wheel. This will bend the shaft. Always hold the bucket wheel
still and unscrew the nut [@usgs_meterma].
:::

### Annual Maintenance

1. Disassemble the meter completely: remove bucket wheel, shaft, and
   pivot.
2. Clean all parts with a lint-free cloth dampened with instrument oil.
3. Inspect the shaft for straightness by rolling on a flat surface.
4. Replace worn or damaged parts.
5. Reassemble and adjust the pivot per the manufacturer's instructions.
6. Perform a spin test to verify performance.
7. Record maintenance date, parts replaced, and spin test results in
   the instrument log [@usgs_meterma].

### Pivot Adjustment

1. Hold the meter inverted with the pivot pointing up.
2. Release the keeper screw and unscrew the pivot-adjusting nut a few
   turns.
3. Advance the pivot-adjusting nut until it touches the yoke.
4. Set end play to approximately 0.001 in -- the shaft should have just
   barely perceptible vertical play detectable by feel.
5. Tighten the keeper screw to lock the adjustment.

### Storage

- Store meters in their waterproof carrying cases.
- Loosen the raising nut to relieve pressure on the pivot.
- Ensure meters are clean and lightly oiled.
- Store in a dry location away from dust and vibration.
- If a meter will not be used for more than 3 months, remove the bucket
  wheel assembly and store separately.


## Rating Tables

Each meter ships with a USGS-approved standard rating table that
converts bucket-wheel revolutions per second to velocity in ft/s or
m/s [@rantz1982; @turnipseed2010]. Keep a laminated copy in each
meter's carrying case and a digital copy on the lab shared drive.

- Type AA rating table: <https://prph2o.com/usgs-type-aa-current-meter/>
- Pygmy rating table: <https://prph2o.com/usgs-pygmy-current-meter/>

### Meter Calibration Verification

USGS studies have found that approximately 35% of Type AA meters and
20% of Pygmy meters in routine field use fail to meet standard rating
criteria, typically because of worn pivots, bent shafts, or damaged
contacts [@rantz1982]. The spin test (§7.2) is the primary field check.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem                       | Probable Cause                  | Corrective Action |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:------------------|
| Spin time below minimum       | Dirty or worn pivot; bent shaft; dry bearings | Clean pivot; inspect for burrs; oil bearings; replace pivot or shaft if damaged |
| Counter not registering       | Loose cable; worn cat-whisker; dead counter battery | Check cable; replace contact wire; replace battery |
| Bucket wheel wobbles          | Bent shaft or frame             | Replace shaft; if hub wobbles, replace bucket wheel assembly |
| Meter reads high              | Magnetized pivot; worn bearing  | Demagnetize pivot; replace pivot bearing |
| Meter reads low               | Excessive friction; over-oiled  | Clean and re-oil; replace pivot if burred |

## Training Record

Before handling or using current meters independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) training
3. Observe a trained operator assemble, spin-test, and clean both meter
   types
4. Successfully perform assembly and spin test under supervision
5. Read [SOP-F301](SOP-F301-stream-discharge-measurement.qmd) before
   using meters in the field
6. Be signed off by the PI or designated trainer
